Perfect. I paid a few bucks more to purchase from Chubbiestech based on a review and to avoid any problems. (Reading about the A10 reviews was scaring me until I realized I was reading the wrong product lol.) This is for the Samsung Galaxy S10e. Being from the S- product line, it's Samsung's flagship product and you can read the history and differences between the models on Wikipedia. I found this information very helpful.

I lucked out with the right Seller and got a phone that really seems brand new and works excellent in every way. (A previous purchase of a different model and seller was excellent in every way but then we discovered it wouldn't charge.) I'm so happy I bought this!

Pros

Mine was in new condition without a scratch, and functions perfectly in every way. I was able to load SmartSwitch on my old J7 and only had to manually download a matching icon set (and create a new Samsung account to download it.) Everything else (including my custom wallpaper from an outside source) transferred exactly.

I wanted a smaller profile/screen because I really loved my J7 and can easily operate it with one hard. I find modern phones too large and heavy and I'm not a gamer. The S10e's profile is surprisingly *smaller* than the J- series and fit my desire. Could easily fit inside a shirt pocket.

It runs way faster than my old phone and I verified with DevCheck that it does indeed have 6 Gigs of Ram. That's more than I ever had before and so it seems real speedy and capable to me and also 128 Gigs of space is way more than I ever thought of using.

I mostly only use my phone as a music source and the sound quality thru my headphones is superb, like my J7 which I prefer to the modern soundboards that I have to tweak; I don't have to use the equalizer on this and the bass is great.

The Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, screentouch and call quality (and charging) all work great. The mobile data connection on my old sim for some reason is much faster (30M??) on 4GLTE and the upload speed is 3x my old phone too, I can't imagine why. But the connection with the same service is just stronger and has much better coverage. I didn't realize it was the old phone limiting it. That's like broadband over 4G lol.

I simply slipped in my old Sim and it connected with no problem or troubleshooting.

Anyway the S- series hardware of this phone is superb. Mine came with Android 12 which I understand is the highest available for this model. My J7 was stuck in Android 8. I didn't want to upgrade to a phablet nor pay a lot for features I didn't want to begin with.

Caveats/Tips

I never used a case before but this phone is so small (yay!) AND slippery I needed to buy a case. Don't want to drop it and scratch the screen because my big clumsy fingers can't hold onto it. I don't have a problem navigating the screensize.

Had to manually customize icons after installing everything. This requires a Samsung account. (You can delete it from Accounts afterward if you wish.)

If you use Smart Switch to transfer and duplicate your experience from your old phone you need to unpair the devices listed under Bluetooth and re-pair them for them to work on your new phone.

Many/Most of your programs transferred and websites will require you to log-in again (so you'll need your passwords) but the data (pics/docs/program files) transferred without a hitch. (You can download Smart Switch on your old phone from Google Play.)

My phone has the annoying T-mobile start-up screen (less annoying if you turn the sound off) but it doesn't harm anything functionally.

Samsung apps preinstalled cannot be uninstalled or disabled. However Google apps can be.

The battery is small (3100) but I'm used to that from the J7. I tried a larger capacity battery in my J7 but became impatient with the charging time so actually prefer the quick charging of these.

This review is obviously for folks who may not have done this before or are doubtful about the quality of the renewed product.

I'm totally happy with the new phone and the process of setting it up was seamless. Definitely worth it and you saved a lot of money! (Now you can peruse the internet and modern apps like the Joneses! :)

Update: It's a bit too small to be honest, and very SLIPPERY, however still prefer this to the large ones. Wish they still made J-size. But everything works great, sounds great and I'm getting 50M download on LTE! All I do is listen to music so it's fine for my needs. Great price for a fast phone.

very good phone for the price, Samsung bloatware is easier to deal with than in past years Now that the price on this phone has gone down to $600, it is a very good deal for the price.

The Snapdragon 865 processor is more than fast enough for anything I want to do. 6GB of memory is less than some other phones in this price range, but it is still more than enough for most people.

The phone feels very solid despite the plastic back. If you use any kind of case, you won't even notice the plastic back.

The phone supports 25W fast charging, but for some reason they only included a 15W charger in the box. Buying the 25W charger separately is a waste of money as well as a waste of the natural resources that were used on the 15W charger. Amazon sells decent 25W fast chargers for less than $15, so cheaping out on the charger is a real lame move by Samsung. You can search Amazon for 15W chargers that support "USB-C PPS" mode and are UL Certified.

The screen looks beautiful when you turn on the 120Hz mode. This does burn your battery more quickly, but the battery is big enough that it still lasts all day.

The screen has been very responsive to me. I have read bug reports about screen glitches for some people. Samsung has already released bug fixes that hopefully have fixed this. I advise only buying this phone from an authorized dealer with no hassle returns so you don't have to worry about this bug.

The phone does have a lot of Samsung bloatware. I owned a Samsung S-series phone several years ago and the bloatware was really bad then. This one is much better. You don't even need to create a Samsung account to use the phone now. Most of the Samsung bloatware (other than the camera app) won't work if you don't have a Samsung account, but if you never use it, this isn't a problem. There are several tutorials online about disabling all the bloatware if you never want to see any of it on your screen.

The triple camera setup on this phone is very good for this price level. The telephone camera works great up to 3X in good light. Image quality deteriorates quickly if you zoom in past 3X or in lower lighting conditions. Telephoto cameras are getting rare in this smartphone price range, so I'm glad this phone has one. I really like using the telephoto lens for landscape and nature photography. The normal and wide angle cameras work better in lower light situations (including indoor situations), though not as good as the iphone or Google Pixel phones. Pictures do tend look more processed than with some other phone cameras. Some people like the Samsung look. Other people prefer more natural looking photos. You should try to look at sample photos before buying the phone, since you cannot completely disable the Samsung photo processing.

This phone comes with Android version 10 out of the box, which is one version behind the Android version 11 that the Google Pixel phones are shipping with. Samsung promises software support with 3 version updates, but that is a little misleading since 1 of those version updates will be just to catch up with the current Android version 11. Still, 3 years of bug fixes and security patches is better than what Samsung used to offer.

It's not the most seamless Samsung experience, but damn if it isn't the best I've run across TL;DR - hardware amazing, software you'll like it or you won't, battery life is inconsistent, let's talk "cinema quality" from the ads

Inconsistent battery life /charging speeds - when I first got this, we're talking 19 hours of me using it. That was impressive. Screen on time in the 6+ hour range, I could kill it if I tried but I'm a psycho power user. Somewhere around month 2 that dropped to finding myself needing to charge after I got home from work, where I wasn't using it.

Your battery life is screen on time, power used to do WiFi or Cell transmission and how much of that you're actually doing, whether you're actually doing anything. Battery should have been nearly full.

Cut to this past week, right back to all day power, with standard usage. Nothing tends to show in the battery usage summary, due to my rather unexciting life I'm usually in the same two places so it's not like I'm dealing with a lot of variables here. Something's up with their power management and here's the other thing I didn't mention - my wife has the same phone. The same issues popped up on hers and we don't really share software in common other than the basic Samsung and Google sets that come preinstalled.

Probably firmware as no battery usage for apps seemed untoward.

Next, this "cinema quality" 8K advertising nonsense. Nah, this is quite a few more pixels than that. 8K is surprisingly not a good experience. You'll be shooting it and it's jerky to watch on screen while shooting, and the end results are - they're good, but looking closely it's just better than 4K, not a whole lot clearer, not a whole lot of effective pixel addition. The codec seems to be set at "awww, they're never going to notice that" as opposed to "save all the image datas!"

The camera is extremely disappointing I bought this phone specifically for the 10x optical zoom camera. This phone is actually really good and the physical hardware is great except for one major flaw. The camera software.

It applies SO MUCH extreme over-sharpening and noise reduction that I have to scale the image down to about 20% scale for it to not look like crap, and even then, some artifacts from the extreme over-sharpening are still visible. As a result, it is incapable of capturing fine details. Also it over-saturates photos a rather extreme amount. And on top of all of that, it saves as somewhat low quality jpegs. Everything about the photos the camera takes is extreme. Extreme zoom, extreme resolution, and extremely crappy.

If you want this phone for everything else it offers, then it's great. It just does a really bad job at taking photos compared to every other smart phone I've had in the past even though none of those phones had optical zoom and only had 8MP or less cameras.

edit: I've since bought a Pixel 5 Pro. Even though it's zoom is only 4x instead of 10x, it doesn't destroy the photos it takes with insane post processing, so it actually manages to capture more detail with only 4x optical zoom than this phone does at 10x optical zoom.

2 Days: A thick case & the pen are absolute necessities for this GREAT camera...phone OK, so I purchased this phone because of the camera. I had read so much about it and for the first time in forever I was tempted to change from my 3rd edition of the Galaxy 7 Active (I have replaced mine 3 times because I like that phone so much as it has actual buttons so there is a smaller chance of inadvertently hitting the screen and initiating an unintended action and will hold up to my actions). That phone took really good photos, but it still couldn't come close to my 35mm camera. This one does and it has options unheard of in a SLR camera.
The photos attached are a great example. If you have had puppies you know how absolutely difficult it is to get a photo because they move so much and so quickly. With this camera...er phone....it takes about 10 frames before the shutter is engaged so even if he moved, I was able to go through the frames and select the one that got him before he moved. The first photo was the beauty shot that I wouldn't have had as he moved right as I clicked the shutter. I was able to get it from reviewing the motion photo and the frames right before I clicked. Similarly without that option I wouldn't have captured photos 2 or 3 or 4 as he was in motion as I shot every single one of those photos. How many times have you said, rats he moved when taking a photo? Particularly if you are shooting animals or children you know you are just as likely to miss the great shot you see in your lens because in the second it takes you to react and shoot, they move. Whoever came up with this motion photo that captures a bunch of frames before you click is a genius.
I have started watching YouTube videos because this camera is in many ways a completely new and different way of taking photos and video. Oh and if you want to select a frame from your video and turn that into a jpeg photo, you can do so.
I am really excited to take my walks this summer. I love macro shots of flowers and bugs, as well as sky shots when a storm is coming in. I typically select the best 10 or so shots taken over the summer in my daily walks to share with others in the area. With this phone I should have even better results. I won't have to go into the neighbor's yards to get up close vegetation shots as the zoom on this is unreal.
I find I use my phone more and more as a substitute for a tablet and with this phone I can see that I may do so by choice. It may be primarily intended to make phone calls but for most the functions are so good that it may do far, far more than that.
The pen and a case with a thick edge are absolute necessities. It is so much easier to navigate the page with the pen and with the pen you don't leave fingerprints. As I am using the screen to review photos, keeping it clean is a must. I have had Samsung pens come with a Chromebook and wasn't impressed, but with this one you will need to watch a separate video on just the functionality of the pen.
A case is needed both to stop inadvertent clicks as your fingers curve around the phone holding it and to enable you to hold it more steady when shooting photos/videos. I tried it without the case and it was a bust. I have nerve damage and can't feel the ends of 5 of my fingers and have nasty arthritis on top of that. The case will also protect the phone when I drop it and I will drop it, that is a given. Holding the phone resulted in numerous inadvertent clicks around the edge. There is an app you can download to create an edge border that will not be effected by touch but I would rather keep the edges as is and grab hold of a case. (I tried the app and it did help, but I felt it took up to much of that beautiful display).
I would also recommend a screen protector. It seems like a no brainer to me as screen breakage is the number one needed repair to cell phones and even with gorilla glass if you are constantly carrying this, getting it in and out, etc. you are going to strike that screen.
Oh and the camera makes good calls as well.....I mean the phone does!
I will update later, but if you are a novice there are a ton of YouTube how to videos available to teach you how to operate this and I would recommend that you go for it, particularly if you are like me a lover of photography. With this phone Samsung has truly changed the way you can obtain high quality images as well as providing a fantastic editing program to work with after you take the shot.

Increased performance, photo, & video - decreased bat. life I had the Moto G7 Power 2019 version, and I bought this version to upgrade that older phone. Overall, Motorola makes a great phone; some people would say this is a "budget phone", but to me, it doesn't feel like it at all.

The pictures come out very clear and detailed, the videos are very good quality (mp4), the phone is very fast - even with multiple apps open at once, etc.

The only thing I've noticed that is a slight difference (in performance) is the battery life. The 2019 model definitely lasts longer than this one; however, the 2019 model also does not take as good of pictures or videos, and it also is nowhere near as fast, so everything is a trade-off.

Overall, I really like this phone. A buddy of mine was looking to upgrade his phone, and I recommended this one to him (he used mine to get a feel for it), and he bought one as well, and likes it as well.

In my opinion, you really can't go wrong with this phone, as long as you're just looking to use it to use Maps, texting, simple web browsing (like looking at Amazon for something to buy for example), taking pictures or videos, etc.

I run Linux (Xubuntu 20.04 LTS), and this phone connects seamlessly to my computer. All I have to do is select "File Transfer" from the notification drop-down item, and it shows up without any issues.

I also helped my buddy set up his phone, and he runs Windows 10, and this phone connected just fine to that as well.

If this review helped you, please give me a thumbs up. Thanks

Solid phone if you realize what you're getting... The G6 is a good phone for the price so long as you're realistic and don't try to compare it to a $900 flagship phone from another brand. For $299 (or barely more than half that when it goes on sale), you are getting a 6+ inch 1080p screen, 4 gigs of RAM, and 64 gigs of internal storage with the ability to add more via a micro SD card slot. It will work on pretty much any carrier (GSM or CDMA), the battery will get you through a work day, and while it only has one speaker, it still is pretty loud compared to many. I'll just toss a few highlight of my own in since it's already been reviewed by tons of people:

PRO: Good screen though not as bring as the G5 for comparison. 70% on this = 50% on the older G5, but still ok once you crank it up.

PRO: Cameras are not great, but good. HDR is improved over past models, detail if more than fine enough for social media and 4x6 prints. The portrait mode (background blur) could be improved but works MOST of the time.

PRO: Call reception at least in my area is good. Decent speaker and headphone jack lets you use corded headsets.

CON: Wifi can sometimes kick off and you have to re-connect it. Random and not often, but worth watching.

CON: No NFC, meaning if you want to store a credit card in it to wave over store terminals to pay for something, you're out of luck. It's turned on with the European models of this, but off on U.S. models (Booooo Moto).

CON: Moto slow with Android updates. This comes with Android 9.0 - expect maybe one major update and a few security updates over 2 years (or so) and that's it.

CON: Has a glass back but no wireless charging, so, it's fragile. Get a good case and use screen protectors.

So again - this is NOT an $800-$1,000 phone, but it comes ridiculously close to most of their features for one-third the price. I think for many people if they spent some time with this, they'd find it suits their needs just as well and could save some money. Look for sales.

ITS A LENOVO PHONE! + 6 MONTHS UPDATE What a disappointment! My first Motorola phone in years have let me down.

Let's talk about the pros:

1) Decent small bezel screen with good resolution, 18:9 ratio is chic!

2) Almost stock Android experience, if vanilla is your favorite flavor.

3) Built in Amazon Apps can be disabled, like you won't know it's there.

4) The Moto gestures are cool, you can activate camera app by twisting your hand twice while holding the phone. Make a chopping motion twice activates flash light. And you can use the fingerprint sensor to navigate the phone instead of your usual on screen buttons.

5) A turbo charger is included, you can charge your phone in under an hour from 0 to 100 easily. But I think I know why it has one bundled with it...Keep reading...

Moving on to the cons, oh boy it's a long one:

1) This is the LOW-SPEC version, other market gets 4gb of ram and 64gb of storage, as well as actual glass back. This one gets 3gb/32gb and a plastic build. Yuck!

2) This phone will only get one more major Android release, the current 8.0 operating system is soooooooooooo damn slow on this phone. Like it becomes sluggish once you have a few apps open. It reminds me of using earlier Android phones. Ah, the nostalgia!

3) Camera sucks despite being a "now in season" dual cam setup. And here are MULTIPLE REASONS WHY IT SUCKS.

A, The Moto camera app takes forever to take a picture.

B, It doesn't have OIS, so all your pictures WILL be blurry. You better be steady like you have three legs (like a tripod).

C, The stock Google photo app takes FOREVER to open the picture you've just taken. Vanilla is not always good!

D, The pictures taken by default tend to be oversaturated, everyone look like they have an orange tan. As my friend puts it, the way this camera renders color is like a flip phone from the early 2000s. UNACCEPTABLE!

4) This one nails it in the coffin, the BATTERY LIFE IS APPALLING! The battery barely lasts a day, even if you use it lightly over time, like just checking emails and using uber apps. I usually unplug my phone at 7AM, and by 2PM I find myself having to reach for the charger. Charging the phone slowly using a standard USB charger does make the battery last a smidge longer. However, I now know why it came with a turbo charger, because you'll be needing to charge this phone quite frequently!

In conclusion,
DON'T BUY THIS PHONE if you have other choices, a similarly priced Huawei or Nokia will perform better than this fraud of a Motorola (Hint: It's actually made by lenovo, which sucks at making phones if you don't already know).

UPDATE 1 (1 MONTH): I've had this phone for over a month and it did not hold up well. I'm experiencing severe hiccup and slow down, especially when trying to use the phone after unlocking the screen. This really is the worst.

UPDATE 2 (6 MONTHS): THE WORST PHONE I'VE EVER HAD! It would now randomly reboot, stops reading SD card until I reboot twice. Each reboot takes 5 minutes. Now its even having difficulty charging! I've already tolerated its short battery life, but now it sometimes won't charge. Battery life sometimes goes down when charging! WTF?!

Well, by now you will ask, Why didn't I just get another phone? To be honest, I simply didn't have money for another phone. I am stuck with this POS until I can buy another phone.

Excellent performance great price I lost other phone (Samsung Galaxy 7) and needed an immediate replacement, so I bought this phone as one of the least expensive ones I could get at Best Buy (I tried to buy the model below this, but it was not able to set up with Verizon). In any case, I actually like this phone better than the Galaxy 7. Maybe it's the fact this uses Android 8 rather than 7, or that it's a new phone, but I finally think this phone breaks the pattern I've had of trying to get the latest and greatest phone every two years or so. I will definitely buy this phone or its replacement when I needed to upgrade the phone. It has decent speed and with an SD card, I have more than enough memory. Moto adds very little junkware as compared to Samsung, so the Android experience is much cleaner. (And it adds a feature that I use all the time-- shaking the phone to use the flashlight.)

Though this doesn't do wireless charging, it has a quick charge feature, and I find it lasts longer than the Galaxy 7.

Mine even came with a decent screen protector already installed, so no bubbles. Oh hes, and the call quality is decent, which is the most important thing since this is a phone.

Dollar for dollar this is the best phone I've had--an inexpensive phone with decent performance. I've only had it a month, but the quality feels very good, and the best thing is that even if I needed to buy another phone in two years, it is far less expensive than getting the latest flagship. I don't feel like this is a second class phone since I like it better than my Galaxy 7 which I believe cost me about $600-$700 two years ago.

Poor voice and LTE signal reception I bought this device direct from Motorola. This is the 3rd phone I've owned in the Motorola G family. The first was the original G7, the second the 2019 version of the Motorola G Power and the third... was this one, the Moto G Power (2021 edition). I expected incremental improvements but I was fundamentally wrong.

The camera continues to suck and its AI is laughable - especially at night. Compared alongside an iPhone XS Max the difference is day-and-night (especially night) with the iPhone taking so much better photos that I eventually dug out my old iPhone 7 to create some context. The iPhone 7 was significantly superior except in terms of native resolution. In particular the iPhones are better at scene composition/lighting and target focusing.

However this wasn't the worst problem. I found the radio reception (voice and LTE) was very marginal and inferior to ALL other Motorola G series phones I've owned to-date. In marginal areas, where the G7 produced crystal clear voice and decent LTE speeds (comparable to the iPhone XS Max) the Moto G Power (2021) was unable to make a voice connect and there was 'no internet' reported (aka no LTE).

So ONE MONTH after I bought the Moto G Power (2021) I wanted rid of it. I thought maybe I could trade-in with Motorola, but no, the phone isn't on their list of applicable trade-ins. I can guess why! So I'm very disappointed with Motorola. I was hoping to trade up to the Motorola One 5g ace, but with no trade-in path for a brand new phone I wasn't going to cough up full price replacing what is essentially a product dud.

I should say that in strong signal areas the Moto G Power (2021) worked fine, both voice and data, so I have to suspect that Motorola made design compromises to extend battery life (which, btw, is superb).

Finally I should add that most of the Motorola phones (at the lower and mid levels) come with Android 10 which is already out-of-date. I suspect this has something to do with memory. The Moto G Power (2021) comes with 4G of RAM but perhaps Android 11 prefers more? Honestly don't know.

So overall this phone has only two strong points. The amazing battery life and the relatively speedy processor (considering it's a low end product). But these can't compensate for a fundamental deficit in radio/data communications. If you want a long battery life I'd recommend you get the 2019 version of this phone which works fine for radio/data and has almost no drawbacks compared to the 2021 version.

*Stock Android (HUGE pro)

*You get a LOT for your money

Not so hot for actually making and receiving phone calls, ok for most other things This is both the absolute worst and in some ways one of the better phones I ever owned. Its good at everything except actually making and receiving phone calls. I can be next to my wife, who is using an iPhone, and she has a signal (phone and internet, carrier or wifi) and I do not. Answering a call is sometimes impossible because the screen does not consistently respond to swipes and the option to use the volume up button is useless if the phone is in a case. There is no option, due to Samsung anti-consumer stupidity, to answer a call by tapping on the answer icon. The phone has only meh facial and thumbprint recognition. So if you want a hand held entertainment device with reasonably fast performance and an OK screen this is the phone for you. If you need a phone to be a phone, not so much. I even sent this clunker in to Samsung when it was under warranty, they said it was working fine. So unless this particular phone is dud I kind of think this may be a systemic Samsung issue: I'll never buy another Samsung phone, I wouldn't even take one as a gift, that's how bad it is.

Bought Used, Glad I did. I generally use an Apple product but a couple days ago found out an SE2022 will not survive the Sanitary cycle of my LG front loading machine.  So I tried this product. Just like the smaller phone.  The photos are nice, larger.  I bought this in "acceptable" condition, used saving about 260 from the list price.  It is worth it.  I would not want to spend list for it though.  I just don't use the additional features.

Mediocre Phone I am offering this review after owning the Galaxy S10E for about 1 year.
I got this phone after I dropped my Moto X in water and I chose the Galaxy because I have a Galaxy watch and they two are supposed to work best together.
I don't particularly have any complaints about the phone, it makes and receives calls. Runs the Android Apps that I find essential. It has reasonable storage.
The Moto X have functions to turn on the flashlight (shake the phone) and camera (twist the phone) that I still miss In fact, when I DO need the flashlight, I find it very cumbersome to turn on as it is a button on the pull-down settings menu.
THe Galaxy has a power share function so I should be able to charge my Galaxy watch from the phone. This does work, however, you have to lay the watch on the BACK of the phone - perfectly centered and STILL. I've had the phone in an Otterbox case the whole time I've had it and when I did need this powershare function, I had to take the phone out of the case. The screen got scratched all to pieces the one time I tried to do this - when I went on a short trip and forgot my watch charger. So, I wouldn't recommend using that function unless you can closely control the environment and ensure the phone doesn't get bumped and is laying on a soft and very clean surface.
It is a small phone - I don't have complaints about the screen per se, but when I hold it out of the case I feel like it might slip through my hands easily.
I have dropped it a number of times - in that Otterbox case - and it has never cracked or failed in any way.
I've mentioned the case a couple of times so I do want to make a disclaimer - I won't buy another Otter Box case - it is supposed to have a lifetime warranty and the corner of it is broken off...I did say that I've dropped the phone, but that corner fell off at the strangest time - in fact, I got into my car and there was a piece of blue plastic lying on my black seat after looking all around, I realized it had come off my phone case. When I contacted the manufacturer they asked me to pay them $6 or $8 to ship a new one. That doesn't seem like much of a warranty to me.
Regarding the interaction with the Galaxy watch: The Wear app doesn't do much. It will help you find the watch if it's lost in the house. Mostly it offers you about a million different watch faces - there's a whole section of the app dedicated to the watch face. As far as functionality, it's very hard to find apps for the watch thru that app.

The Hype is Legit. Device from USA Miami, Florida Not some Chinese Knock-off Everything on this phone is superb so far. I actually ordered two (and as can sometimes happen, the 2nd phone would NOT come on at all. LOL. That one was returned, and I decided instead to get a 4G tablet for my 2nd device). But for the 1st phone the Blu G9 Pro set up was a breeze. Stuck the TMobile simcard and it worked instantly--could make calls, surf, and sms texting. 4G signal consistent. Screen is bright, crisp, colorful. Speakers are adequate. Device response is fast and accurate. No lags. Videos and music smooth. Battery life so far is good (also bought a wireless charging hub that I placed on my nightstand--no more wires during bedtime and alarm-clock mornings!) and fast charge is really, really great. The included case and screensaver the phone came with is nice and will seem to keep the phone safe for now; they also look to be good quality just like the phone, which has nice glass, sturdy design. For a guy I am not very much into the flashy-fancy patterns but for this phone I am loving the colors and design on it. Seems very well-made but the glass on the back makes me nervous of accidence. There is one heavy duty case I found here on Amazon that I also ordered.

I think Blu has done a tremendous job in enginnering this device. I am ALSO glad Blu is an American company and the phone came from Miami, Florida (or at least assembled there...obviously some or most parts are imported)...which means you are NOT getting some cheap Chinese knock-off scam. You are getting a wonderfully legit smartphone that rivals if not is better than iPhone II Pro...that is if price and expandability is factored into the comparison (you cannot add an SDcard with iPhones). It could just be that I am a previous "Blu Virgin" but I am kind of surprised I have not stumbled on a few of these phones in public already, especially for how well-made, designed, and appropriately priced they are...it is no brainer to buy Blu G9 Pro over any of the other $1k or so phones in the market. Blu should definitely go more mainstream beyond Amazon marketplace and hopefully they keep with the same durable design and affordable prices in the future.

I will update in a month or two if the phone holds up to my momentary glee and satisfaction.

Not for power users. Subpar battery As a diehard Samsung fan, i really wanted to love this phone. The spec sheets speaks to cost cutting measure to try to release a device while also upgrading some minor components from last years release.

For the pros
-Great form factor. Very easy to yield in one hand and much more comfortable to hold compared to an iPhone 13.
-Nice vivid screen with variable refresh. Some ppl will not notice much a difference in day day use. The phone will feel faster and smoother when navigating through menus or webpages. Video content tends to run at 60 fps so you won't notice much for a difference in media consumption.
-Lightweight. The combination of aluminum and glass made this device much easier to yield.
-Great UI and customization. Samsung leads the way with being to change everything from fonts, icons, tile placements, themes. Very robust options and some are available for free via thier Samsung store

Cons- Terrible battery. Most reddit posts and reviewers will tell you to disable or throttle services to get it to last all day. But why pay for features that you can readily get at a fraction pf the price or cheaper (Like a pixel 5a or a Zenphone 9).
- Thermal throttling issues. May not he a big issue for you but extensive gaming will render the phone hot to the touch. It appears the passive cooling on the device has either been taken away or not implemented in a way to help mitigate heat away from the hands
-Unoptimized OS/Hardware. Something about this release feels rushed. I experienced terrible standby time (phone died unused in my pocket at a wedding venue in 8 hours). Apps would generally freeze or force close.

At its msrp, this phone is a hard pass. At 700, there are much better devices with better performance both in battery and software. If youre looking at this price range, consider a Pixel 5a (not the 6 as Tensor is still buggy), Zenphone 9, or even an Apple 13/ 13Mini

Doesn't get much better than this! I currently have a Galaxy Note 10 and before that the Pixel 3. The Note 20 has been great but I've been wanting to upgrade to something with a better battery. I've tried the Note 20 Ultra (too big and bulky) and the Note 20 (not worth $999 or even $799) and finally arrived at the S20 FE. So far, the battery life has been great with 6-7 hours screen on time.

Compared to the Note line and pretty much everything else in the marketplace right now, this is a fantastic device at this price point. The screen is as good as the Note 20 line with its great color accuracy, sharpness and bright screen. While it doesn't have WQHD+ like the Note 20 Ultra, it does have 120hz which the Note 20 doesn't. So if you're running 120hz, you can't use WQHD+ anyway.

This device also has a fantastic camera system that takes better shots than the Note 20. I've compared them side by side and the S20 FE delivers more vibrant and sharper images. While the telephoto is only 8MP, it didn't seem to effect the quality and outputs pictures that were just as good as the Note 20. The Note 20 Ultra has an amazing telephoto, so if that's important to you, then go for it, but costing about $500 more than this device, seems not worth it.

If you're a Pixel user, One UI is an adjustment but I actually enjoy it with all the options it brings. Unlike past Samsung devices, their OS doesn't slow things down in the least and this phone is as fast as the Note 20's that I also tried out. Samsung has also been great about doing monthly updates and will be giving 3 years OS support on the S20 FE

I do wish it came with 8GB instead of 6 but I haven't noticed any performance issues as a result - the device feels just as fast and fluid as the other more expensive phones I tried with much more RAM. Perhaps if you're a gamer or heavy multi-tasker, this might be a bigger factor to consider in your decision to buy this device.

I've seen comments about the finger print scanner being unreliable but I haven't experienced that at all. In fact, it's been much more reliable and way faster than sonic ones in the newer Note 20 devices I tried.

If you're considering this over the Pixel 5, the S20 FE seems the better value with better CPU, 120hz screen and more versatile camera system (but the Pixel will undoubtedly take better pictures as its the camera king!), expandable storage, bigger battery and faster charging.

If you're considering this over the Note 20 (standard not Ultra), the S20 FE is a much better value for less money giving you 120hz screen, expandable storage and better camera. Unfortunately you lose out on the S-Pen with the S20 FE, but if you can go without, then the S20 FE is a much bigger bang for your buck.

At the end of the day, I think this phone is a superb value at $599 and the best you can get at this price point.

Quality Cell without spending $$$$$ I purchased the Moto G6 on June 6 after reading about the Nokia 6.1, LG cells.. So I've had time to use the cell and give a review based on usage - not just a first week excitement viewpoint. I do like the cell and it has done what I what though sometimes not as automatically as I would like. See #2 below.
There are many things to like and several things of which to be aware.

Cons
1) The moto G6 has many many apps that can NOT be deleted. They can be disabled, but not deleted. You are stuck with them. So your 32 GBs is more like 18 GBs for your music, photos, etc. You can add memory if needed.
2) From time to time (ghosts?) the sounds you select for receiving texts or phone calls gets turned off. I have no explanation for how this happens. Fortunately the alarm clock sounds have always gotten me up!!

PROS
1) price - I paid $235.00
2) 3 GB RAM
3) 5.7 HD screen - good size
4) great images
5) Battery life - this is subjective - I charge it each night and always have 30 - 50 % left at the end of the day. I also dont have it "on" easch minute of the day. It turns off after a couple of minutes of non-usage.
6) Fingerprint recognition
We all have our personal uses for our cells. Very good cell. Go for it.

Loving it so far I was waiting for the Pixel 5 which came out the same time. The 5 was $100 more ($699) than Amazon's price of S20 FE of $599 at release (*S20 FE now $699) with the 5 using processing power of a few generations back with smaller battery capacity - this was a no brainer choice and Google over priced their flagship (I understand their camera is generally good and updates faster/ui cleaner - but that's not making up for everything else especially considering competition from this phone and OnePlus among others).

It's still brand new so time will tell a lot more but the phone is snappy and my wifi & cell signal are faster than my Honor View 10 that's being replaced. I use T-mobile and not in a 5G area yet (but one is close by I'll be able to test). I attached a pic of my speed test info on cell network. The bottom 2 similar results are default with 5G enabled in the cellular settings and the top (fastest) results is with the second option of 4G LTE/3/2 enabled. I thankfully read a post to disable 5G if not in network for one. My old phone would only get 25 download on average so the S20 FE has blown that away even at its worst.

I took a photo in an average edge lit room of some colored items and a pic in a very low light room (any light coming in is from a room at least 10ft away). I'm blown away by the low light pic - I can't explain how well lit the pic is compared to what my eyes perceive.

The first day I spent my time uninstalling and disabling whatever I could that was pre-installed by Samsung and tweaked shortcuts & and new to me (Samsung specific) features I wanted. I used the recommended Smart Switch to transfer files from my old phone (namely apps, selected pics, and texts & call records) and I used my saved backup from my launcher (Nova) to bring back the app/screen organization I had customized on my old phone. Now I get to enjoy.

It does charge fast and no problems connecting to 2 different Bluetooth headsets.

*Update* I realized my original download speed pic was clipped wrong (showed a 2G wifi download speed instead of LTE) so I removed the old and uploaded correct pic (speed increase still stands).

I placed prices in as they've changed since I purchased.

You can choose to bring your screen refresh to 60 to help extend battery (defaults at 120 - I recommend scrolling feeds and testing both out in other scenarios to see if it's worth it for you). As always, to extend battery on any phone, control background apps and their access, lower your screen brightness when able and keep GPS, wifi, Bluetooth off when not needed. If your phone has bad reception in an area you spend a prolonged period of time in and you don't need to call/text, put your phone in airplane mode and turn wifi on after (if wifi available/needed).

Great phone for the price (a little bulky) The Blu G90 Pro phone works very well and is a steal at the price. Here are (a) positives, (b) negatives and (c) differences between this and the newer G91 phone with similar specs.

(a) Positives
+ Lots of memory and storage
+ Separate slots for 2 SIM cards and 1 SD card all simultaneously
+ Android 10
+ Very high-resolution display 1080x2340
+ Long battery life
+ Rapid charger (but see negatives also)

(b) Negatives
- The bulky case which no doubt cost them more and is a positive for many but it makes the phone heavier and bulkier than it already is
- Rapid charger is not the standard Qualcomm rapid charger and is somewhat slower than the Qualcomm system (but faster than a standard charge). The adaptor says 9V output (only), which suggests that it is not an adaptive 9V/5V "intelligent" charger. If this is true, you probably don't want to use the charger on anything else even though it looks like a standard USB charger as it may burn it out.

(c) Differences from G91

They are more similar than different: Both have 2 SIM + 1 SD card slots, both have 128GB/4GB memory, both have 6.5" screen size and weight and thickness are very similar.

The G90 has the following that the G91 does not:
+ Rapid charging
+ 1080p resolution (G91 has 720p but would be hard to notice the difference)
+ Faster processor (I don't notice the difference but gamers might)
+ Heavy duty black case vs. slimmer silicone case (supposed to be a positive though I prefer the silicone)

Note that the Amazon listing for both G90 Pro and G91 say that they are "not compatible with new AT&T or Cricket activations," but it is not clear how true this is and what "new activation" means (is putting an existing SIM into a new phone a "new activation"?) All I know is that my existing account with AT&T worked just fine with my G90 Pro even though I had to replace the SIM card (I later ported my number to T-Mobile anyway, for unrelated reasons). The reason for this, which I tracked down, is that AT&T is phasing out their 3G network by 2022, so that they are no longer activating new service on phones that do not support Voice over 4G LTE (called VoLTE), which is how all voice will be carried on their network in the future. My G90 has a setting "Enhanced 4G LTE Mode (Recommended)" which I'm guessing is VoLTE. T-Mobile explicitly recognized the IMEI of the phone as being VoLTE-compatible but AT&T does not list any Blu phone in their "official" list of VoLTE-supported phones which, surprise surprise, focusses on phones that AT&T sells. So ... until we can get more clarity on this you may want to choose a GSM carrier other than AT&T or Cricket if you want to use Blu phones.

According to Motorola, this phone does not support wifi calling with Verizon I did not buy this phone from Amazon, though I sort of wish I had. Instead, I bought it directly from Motorola specifically because it is supposed to support wifi calling. I live in what might charitably be called a 'fringe area', which means cell coverage is at best, poor, and often non-existent.

Because of that, I need wifi calling, and when looking for a new phone, this one says it does support wifi. When the phone arrived, I began the process of setting it up but to my frustration, I could not seem to find how to activate wifi calling. I finally called customer service and asked how to enable wifi calling on the phone. I was told that my carrier (which does support wifi calling on my phone plan) does not support wifi calling on Moto G phones. I asked if wifi calling was supported on this model phone by other carriers, and was told that only one supported it.

Basically the Moto G phones seem to be good phones at a reasonable price, but for me, this makes the phone unuseable to a degree that I find unacceptable for my needs. If you do not need wifi calling, it is probably a good choice.

Great phone! Came from an S9 I got my S9 after my S4 crapped out after 5 years (screen went off, wasn't even cracked). My S4 & S9 served me very well! I had the S9 for 4+ years it simply is an amazing phone. I was at a crowded place, and someone knocked my elbow while holding it. It fell, and the screen cracked pretty bad (not like one crack, many cracks). Screen still works perfectly, but, I was scared it could stop working at any time. So, I needed a new phone. I looked at the S21 FE and S22. At the time I purchased, the prices were about $200 different (then a week after I purchased, prices were the same!). But, I'm happy with my purchase. I liked small phones in the past, never had a bigger one. I am actually enjoying the larger screen. Better for viewing content. I'm a guy and my pants pockets are plenty large for this phone as well. Feels no different than my previous S9 in my pocket. I've watched a lot of YouTube reviews of the camera / video quality / test pics and footage, and it seems they are almost the same (sometimes I prefer and think the S21 FE image / video looks better, others the S22 looks better - kind of a toss up).

So, what have I noticed? Well, battery life is amazing! Beats my S9 by FAR! Now, my S9 was 4+ years old when I had to replace it (now use the S9 as a "camera I'm not worried about losing or breaking"). I had the S9 for a long time, and I cannot remember how good battery life was when I first got it. But, I don't recall it ever getting worse either. What I can say is, I used to have to top my S9 up a bit at least once or twice a day. My S21 FE, lasts ALL DAY (and I even have the battery saver setup so it only charges to 85% - never did that with the S9). And even from 85%, I get a full day no problem! Usually around 35% or so when I am ready for bed. The screen is great. I do leave on 120hz mode all the time. I also have dark mode turned on. I like how it looks, and dark things on screen use less battery than bright white things. But yes, battery is great.

Now the cameras. My S9 actually had almost identical video. I make YouTube videos and the S9 did me very well in 4K by 30 or 60. I do notice the S21 FE is ever so slightly better image. It also has better stabilization and just some other processing stuff that helps out. The pictures are better for sure. I've taken pictures of people and shown them, and they've been like, "What phone is that?!? The pictures are sooooo good!" The S9 did well. But, the S21 FE is for sure an improvement. I used to use my G7X Mark ii for most pictures, because it just was better by far than my S9. Now, I don't think I ever really need that camera anymore. This phone produces awesome photos!

I haven't had a single issues, no glitches, no nothing. Just a smooth perfectly working phone. I did kind of like the S9 having the fingerprint reader on the back. But, I quickly got used to the in screen reader. It works fast and great. Apps load fast. Camera is on in an instant with a double tap of the power button. Just really nothing to complain about. I would have kept my S9 another few years, but, I am happy with the S21 FE and hope it lasts me 5+ years as well.

Great phone, if you are looking into it and deciding if you want to get it, I for sure recommend it.

I'll stick to Samsung as long as I can buy refurbs that are 2 years old for 1/4 or less what they cost new.

Perfect. Absolutely beautiful phone. Perfect. Absolutely beautiful phone.

Edit: 05/06/19 Update

I think I originally bought this back in January. It was a solid phone for five months. On a day-to-day basis, I use a Samsung S8 for IT work and this Blu Vivo XL4 for personal use. There were considerable performance differences but as far as how it looked and held up against time, I really think this phone was a phenomenal deal. I would recommend it for anyone that isn't in IT or development or needs a high-performance phone for x, y, and z reasons. This will easily handle social media, netflix, internet browsing, email, etc just fine. It would be a very good phone for the intermediate user. Trust me, unless you are using your phone as a work device on a regular basis, this is an exceptionally valued phone.

* Screen is impeccable, absolutely love it.
* Intuitive design, everything - power buttons and the like - is where it's supposed to be (according to me, lol).
* I had a tempered glass screen protector but it was funky so I removed it and there have been no scratches or cracks on the screen for several months until I dropped it two stories down. It hit every concrete step and then flew a whole story off the apartment stairs. I mean, nothing would have survived that. Not even me. So it was a champ for a very long time.
* Great battery life.
* Wasn't USB-C but it was a fast charge with the right adapter and cable.
* Storage was not enough for me towards the end, but I ended up downloading a lot of stuff inadvertently for work or other productive reasons (microsoft apps and the like) but also for things like Audible and email to voicemail downloads, etc.
* RAM was not enough for me towards the end. I ended up doing a factory data reset just to be sure and as it turns out, I needed a higher spec phone for the things I wanted and needed to do.

This is a great phone. I made my brother jealous and he bought an iPhone X at around the same time that I bought this because the screen was pretty amazing and he paid 9-10x as much for his phone (ouch, brother, ouch).

Again, this isn't going to handle an intensive load very well. It operates under 1.5GB of RAM just for regular OS apps and services, so you're really only working with 1.5GB of free RAM. Honestly, that's enough to do what most people want to do. You don't need a flagship phone anymore to watch youtube or get on social media. We need to move away from that trend. Buy only what you need and the flagship phone manufacturers will start coming down in price - as they should anyways since technology improves over time.

A huge heartbreaker for me was, towards the end, messages and calls weren't being received as often as they probably should have been but my Galaxy would get them with no problem. I would later get them if I sent a text out or made a phone call. The bluetooth stopped working with some but not all of my devices. Not sure what was going on there but I didn't investigate too much. I paid $129 for crying out loud. That's a steal compared to the "more than my rent or mortgage payment" cost of a flagship phone these days.

Overall, I'd recommend it to intermediate users or those who lost a phone and need something in the interim until they have enough money to buy a flagship.

Had 2 fail but loved them regardless LOL Got the purple one, very attractive. It has better features than the Motorola phones I've had, Samsung, too, even the $700 one that I bought refurbished for less than $3oo at the time. The interface is just so much better. Also, Blu responds to my emails very quickly in a HUMAN way. No cut and paste replies so far.

But I had 2 of this model fail, the second (a replacement) only 2 days after owning it. Left the first one in the car overnight and all I can think of is condensation built up inside it (it was so COLD here that night) because it would not turn on again. I dried it out for 3 days with silica packets, still no joy. Amazon did not hesitate to replace it even though it is sold directly by Blu.

The second one stopped detecting my sim and sd card. This (Sd Card not detected) issue happened with my Blu View 2 I bought early this year, though in that case there were visible missing pins in the sd card slot. This one worked fine--for 2 days. I tested the battery health as soon as I set up the phone and there were several bad cells in it. The first phone didn't have this issue. I really wish built-in batteries were outlawed! LOL

So this tells you about the failures I just had.

I did NOT find any bloatware on either one of them as some reviewers complained about. Reboots fairly quickly. Images and text look great. Very nice GUI. Very responsive in NORMAL use. Sound is great, though I play all of my music via Bluetooth speakers, which is paired with easily.

The negatives that are built-in I was willing to accept because I like their phone's GUI setup. No NFC. No wifi calling capability. Ram is limited so games often reboot if you tab over to another running app. Stuck with Android 10 even though Blu was supposed to roll out Android 11 in the 4th quarter according to one person in the questions answered section. Reviews point out that it's theoretically faster than the newer G91 because of a better processor. I think the additional ram would serve me better than the barely slower processor.

But with 2 critical issues with 2 successive phones, I don't think I'm going to get this model again. I'm on a fixed income so my options are just so limited. I'm very sad about this because I actually like the company, just based on their CS responses.

I'm a Samsung fan and professional photographer, but I don't think I would buy this model again This is my fourth Samsung phone. Even though I liked my Galaxy S10, I decided to "upgrade" to this newer model as my backup camera for our 3 month Europe trip, for part of which I was on assignment with a major cruise line. Here's my summary after extensive use:
PROS: The HDR function works amazingly well, which means that in tricky lighting situations, including too much contrast or the opposite gray flat weather, it produces sharp and beautifully colored images. It handles low light situations really well, too. The battery lasts a long time--no idea how long because I charged every night and it never came close to dying.
CONS: Three things bother me: 1. Good buy, no worries, battery health at 100%.. Like some of the other reviewers, I had concern about the condition of a 'renewed' phone. As it turned out, it arrived in perfect, like-new condition. No observable defects, no observable wear/scratches/scuffs even when looking closely, not at arms length as Amazon mentions.

Using the iOS battery health app, the battery health was at 100% when I received it. Amazon advertises that the phone will arrive with at least 80% battery health. To check, go to Settings > Battery > Battery Health and then look at Maximum Capacity. If it shows up in problematic condition, Amazon covers it with a generous 90 day return policy. I suspect that the one I received was an 'instant regret' purchase by the original owner and returned immediately. It seems likely that most 'renewed' phones will have some battery degradation so expecting battery health to be at 100% is unrealistic.

The only issue I had was not related to this phone. Call sound quality wasn't good and drop outs. After doing a network reset, that was fixed. Go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset Network Settings > enter your passcode and then Reset Network Settings (red letters). Your phone will reboot. You'll have to log on to your wifi network again and if you have a VPN, you may have to set that up again. After doing this, no drop outs and good sound quality. Note that the network reset process changed after the iOS 15 update. Going forward, the sequence above may change again.

Amazon's refurb department did a great job of cleaning, wiping the previous installation of iOS and repackaging it. Regardless, I did a complete reset before restoring from a backup. This probably isn't necessary but it brought some peace of mind knowing that It was a clean installation of iOS.

It arrived in a well designed aftermarket box designed for cell phones, an Apple charger, Apple cable and an aftermarket screen protector of the type used for shipping protection. They mention that it may come with an aftermarket charger and cable so don't expect Apple branded accessories.

Presumably most people purchasing the iPhone 12 Mini will have informed themselves of the pros and cons of this model (ahem..battery life). I'd guess that most will not find battery life to be an issue. For heavy users and for those that regularly use high drain features such as GPS navigation, it would be advisable to have charging capability in the car and at work.

The only thing I'd add is that if you want the leather MagSafe case from Apple, keep an eye on prices. It usually sells for 60 dollars but the black one was on sale in Amazon at the time of this writing for 23.99 + tax. Instant purchase and on the way.

I used an Apple leather case with an iPhone 8. I was satisfied with its basic protection, feel and handling. Its unlikely to provide as much drop protection as an Incipio Duo and other cases designed with drop protection in mind but 23.99 + tax was hard to pass up.

Happy customer, solid purchase for an unlocked iPhone.

Wow. What a phone. I’m impressed by how much you get for the price. Pros:
-Screen: Nice and vivid, clear with a high resolution. Doesn’t compare to an OLED, but is quite nice overall. Resolution is high enough that you can set the font to whatever size you like, and it is legible and clear. Oh, and the screen fills ups the profile of the phone nicely- nice to upgrade to a phone that has minimal bezels.
-Battery: Wow! 4000mah! Currently phone was charged 15 hours ago, is at 37%, with 6hr 30min screen on time. Impressive to say the least.
-Quick charger: it charges quickly, which is great for the large battery size. I don’t currently wireless charge, but nice to have in case I decide to get a wireless charger.
-Contents: Comes with a case, screen protector, and headphones that are decent.
-Storage: 128gb! Plenty of space to store everything, and if that’s not enough you can use an SD card to expand.
-Speedy: Was worried about the MediaTek chip, but haven’t had any issues so far. Everything I use has loaded quickly, and works smoothly. I don’t do gaming where supposedly this chip will fall behind; but YouTube plays HD just fine.
-Fingerprint reader: I like the rear placement and am used to it from my previous phone. Quick unlock works great.
-LTE Coverage: Plenty of bands to cover the US GSM network. Works great on T-Mobile.
-Minimal preinstalled junk: Most can be removed, except for Opera, which I disabled.
-Price: $200!!!

Cons:
-Screen: Adaptive brightness is finicky.
-Camera: No obvious way to switch between 20mp, 5mp, and 16mp in Photo mode. Ai “tech” is unclear, and appears to auto switch between cameras as it sees fit. So… thanks for the 3 cameras, but I don’t see much use in them without the ability to change them as needed.
-Volume: jumps between just too quiet to too loud with no in between.
-Headphones: Only play/pause, no up/down.

Other:
-Aggressive multitasking: Was confused by this as I’d be using 1.7gb of ram out of 4, but apps in background constantly would be shut down and would have to reload each time you switched apps. Turns out this is more a problem with Android 9.0- To remedy, go into battery optimization for the app and turn off optimization for apps that you don’t want to clear out.

Nice phone, but slippery and expensive to replace the front glass We just upgraded from our old S7's to these S20's. Love the additional power of the phone, the battery life is easily double the old S7 (even with more frequent use during the day than what we typical did on our S7's). Screen resolution is super, camera is great.

The things we didn't like are:
- the phone is slippery, especially with the curved front glass on the long edges of the phone
- the slim/lightweight style phone cases that protected the S7 won't protect the front glass on the S20, so you either have to never drop your phone, or you have to get a heavy, bulky phone case, which kinda defeats the purpose of having a thin, lightweight phone
- depending on how you're holding the phone, the curved edge can allow the phone to think that your holding fingers are actually trying to touch the screen and get interpreted as finger presses, which can lead to unexpected things happening on the screen or no action at all when you try to press a screen button or scroll with your other hand (because nothing happens since the phone thinks your holding finger is doing something). So you have to hold the phone the 'right way' to make sure the screen works. Unlike Steve Jobs, I don't think you should have to hold your phone a 'certain' way in order for it to work correctly.
- The curved edges make the front glass easy to shatter if you drop it front-glass down (see attached pic). Even with this little damage to the screen, the screen is half white, which makes the phone completely non-functional.
- It costs *more* to replace the screen than to buy a new phone (as of 10/26/22, screen replacement is $270, and the new phone with tax is $230).
- The phone doesn't support a micro-sd card.
- The phone doesn't have the nifty blinking blue/red/green LED on the S7 that let you know if you had a missed call, notification, or low battery. I miss that feature.

So, while it is a great phone and screen, the practical issues involved in everyday use fall short. We can't recommend this phone.

We are now looking at the S20 FE, which has a flat screen like the S7, a plastic backside (unlike the S20's glass backside), which we think will be a much better choice for our needs.

Note that the S20 FE as a new phone cost less than the S20, but the refurb'd FE's cost more than the refurb'd S20's. I think this is the marketplace voting that the FE is a better practical phone than the S20 flagship. And the FE front screen replacement only costs $150, which is a deal since you are much less likely to break the glass on the FE.

You Get What You Pay For I have been using this phone for the past four months. Over the four months, the phone has performed pretty well, but I have had four issues with the phone. First, I want to say that this phone has really good specifications for the price, and it is very aesthetic looking. A great camera, a pretty good screen, and AMAZING battery life. Unfortunately, after four months of use, it is clear to me that software issues will keep this phone from lasting much longer. I will go over those issues below. I have already purchased a new phone, and will start using it once it is delivered to me.

1. CORRUPTED OPERATING SYSTEM: About two months into owning this phone, the screen randomly turned black and a message saying something along the lines of "your android operating system has been corrupted, please click to reinstall". I have never seen this before on a phone, and it really scared me because I would lose a lot of data I don't have backed up. Thankfully, when on this screen, I just restarted the phone without accepting to reinstall android. When the phone restarted, everything was back to normal, and none of my data was gone from my phone.

2. SCREEN FREEZES: I have had this problem twice in it's four months of use. The screen just freezes and becomes unresponsive. The only way to fix the problem is to restart the phone.

3. REALLY WEIRD TIME ZONE SETTINGS: I have had the problem once where the time zone would not automatically set correctly. It would automatically set to be an hour ahead of the actual time. I changed the settings to where I manually set the time, but once I locked the phone screen, the time zone setting would be reset to where it was automatic and an hour ahead, instead of manually set. I had to restart the phone to get it to stop doing this.

4. SCREEN RANDOMLY TURNS ON: In the past four days, my phone screen has been randomly turning on. I do not know why it is doing this because I am not getting any notifications, or anything like that. I have restarted the phone several times since this problem began, and it is not going away.

CONCLUSION: Overall, I think you get what you pay for with this phone. It has some pretty nice features for the price, but it's not built to last. If you want a phone with a good camera and great battery life, but will only last for not even half a year, then this phone is right for you. Otherwise, I would pay the extra money and go with a more reputable brand.

Too clunky, bulky, & clumsy. Powerful, and not worth it. 2 Month Update:

Pros:
-Bright screen
-Bluetooth range improvement
-Camera is good for a phone (better than iPhone's)
-16gb RAM is great for power users, multitaskers, virtual desktops, and casual chrome use.

Cons:
-Exclusively 2-handed operation. It is too big for you to use with one hand. Yes, I do mean you reader, and I do mean that in all cases and in every situation this is too big for 1 handed use. You can't eek by once, or 'good enough' it, it's just plain too big for that.
-No micro SD means that this phone can hold only ~8-10 movies in modern 10-bit 4k HDR format (without any music, apps, photos etc.. installed)
-Large black hole in the screen still draws the eye
-Curved screen edges distort both images and colors along the full length of the phone.
-No way to charge the phone without buying extra hardware.
-120hz screen isn't smooth, it's just marginally MORE smooth than 60hz
-TRUE 5g isn't accessible to 95% of the US market, and won't be for some years yet (as of March 2021).

Overall:
This is an ok, but not great phone. It really is ok. However, I regret buying this phone, and separately regret buying from Samsung. I would not recommend this phone to anyone, and can't think of a single use-case wherein this would be the best phone for you. Maybe if you own exclusively Samsung electronics, $1,400 isn't that much to spend yearly on upgrades (you'll want to upgrade out of this phone asap) and don't own but need a decent (not great) camera. I guess then I still would recommend the Galaxy flip over this so no, there really isn't any good consumer for this product. I ordered this through Samsung, and I was screwed on every level with everything related to this phone except for the phone itself. Every accessory I bought, or didn't recieve, the experience, the customer service, all Comcast-level crooked corrupt corporate thievery (and I'm very pro corpo so... seriously these guys are the worst). Putting all that aside, the S21U phone itself is just OK, which isn't ok at this price.

In more detail:
-Screen brightness allows for screen viewing in most outdoor settings. I was able to see the screen just ok at the beach. If you live in a 'sunny' place, this may not be true for you. Just 3-4% brightness without the blue light filter is eye-searingly bright in the morning, and too bright for night driving for some reference.
-120hz REALLY isn't that noticble 99% of the time. This isn't at all like on a TV or monitor, where the miniscule movements add up to make a very noticble difference in gaming feel or web page scrolling. The improvement between 4k and UHD is much more noticble, even in a phone-sized screen. There is still a ton of blur and shuttering when scrolling menus, better than 60hz doesn't mean it's actually smooth. 60fps videos are where the smoothness is most appreciated. 60fps content is very rare indeed and you only need a 60hz screen to enjoy it. I'll keep 120hz for reaction speed and aiming accuracy on my pc monitors and for console gaming, but it just isn't what I thought it would be here. The vivid colors are more noteworthy than the 120hz screen. I just hear a lot about that 120 number on this phone for what little it actually does.
-There is no way to charge this phone. If you buy extra hardware you can get around this. I know Apple offers USB chargers for around $20 ;)
-Curved screen distorts and discolors at the edges.
-Pinhole camera draws the eye as a stationary and black spot on the otherwise colorful and in-motion images on the screen, making it way more obvious. This doesn't fade with time. I'm still not used to a hole in my screen, and am self-conscious whenever sharing content on the screen with others.
-No micro SD slot means you won't have any storage issues for probably the first year, depending on your use. This is NOT a good media phone, despite the screen. At ~80gb, you can only store five 4k HDR movies (standard modern format) on this, if you have almost nothing else installed. The formatting makes the screen size irrelevant for playback. Fit to screen means the edges are rounded off, the top and bottom are distorted from the curved
-The 'Pro' headphone companions are a joke, and are streets behind apple's airpods.
-This phone is too big. The power is appreciated, but the cellular/wifi bottlenecking (AT&T 5g, and Xfinity wifi 280down, 12up for me) gives that extra umph a minimal effect. The main issue is that this is too heavy for one-handed use. While I normally used 2 hands with my smaller s8+, I SERIOUSLY underestimated the necessity of being able to check something quickly by pulling the phone out and looking at the screen, replying 'ok' while driving, or browsing YouTube while holding a drink. These things are GONE. if it was only the size, one-handed operation would be uncomfortable but possible, here it's just out of the question. I have big hands as a 6'1" 260lb guy, and can't imagine anyone outside of the NBA could reach the far side of the screen with one hand.

--------------------
If you're considering the S21 I would advise waiting for the S22 or fold3. This iteration has a not quite finished design, with issues that will be gone next gen. Most notably, this will be their last flagship to have a punch hole selfie camera in the screen. I use this and my old s8+ in equal measure, as the s8+ is a sleeker, lighter, more comfortable phone. The s21 ultra is a more powerful one. 5g is also a gimmick for the time being, unless you live in a major metropolitan area and have Verizon. ATT 5g is a misnomer and is a faster 4g variant, not actually 5g. This is also for the fast and capable US version with snapdragon 888, exynos s21 ultras are MUCH slower and less efficient.

The screen is good, not great, and has a large hole in it. Yes it is a smoother 120hz, this is more noticeable to me in 60fps video than scrolling, contrary to what others have said they notice. 60fps content is very rare. Battery is significantly better but still doesn't last all day unless it's in your pocket or on battery saver mode.

This is a massive, heavy, thick, two-handed phone. You will not be able to type while holding one handed. This hurts my pinky and ring fingers from supporting it's weight, which is exentuated by how tall it is, throwing the center of gravity way out there. I was shocked by how thick and heavy this is for a cellphone, the biggest I've seen. The hole punch has never been more obvious and it ruins watching anything in full-screen. They battery certainly does not last all day unless on power save mode. The camera is very good. It is ugly. The camera bump means that a case is a must, and it cannot lie flat on a surface. It wobbles when you touch it. Did I mention how thick and heavy this is? I was very excited about this phone but it's honestly just not that good. There are a few nice features (smooth screen, good cam, fast processor) which are totally eclipsed by basic phone necessities that were ignored (too heavy, too thick, battery not enough for what it's intended to power). The fingerprint sensor is ok, that was an issue on s20. It's not entirely reliable, and only capable of storing 4 prints, but is adequate now.

Frequent Bluetooth audio dropoff ruins an otherwise great phone. So, how could I rate its features so high yet rate the phone so low? Bluetooth is an important feature to me and it's been broken since I bought the phone.

Here's the issue: I can be listening to something on my headset or speaker, book or music, and suddenly the audio will cut off and the device will say, "Your headset [speaker] is disconnected." Then ten seconds later it'll say "Your headset [speaker] is connected.. Now, some audio apps can recover from that. Others just stop and need to be started again. It's a massive irritation. To make it worse, it can go three days without happening at all and make me think my latest home remedy corrected the problem. Then, it'll start again. And if it happens once, thereafter it'll do it continually.

On the entire web, I haven't been able to dig up anything about this specific problem (or almost, see below). Some remedies I've tried: contacting customer service, (they had me do a factory reset, a hassle that didn't have any effect on the problem.) I've tried unpairing and repairing. I've tried making sure only one device is paired and having all my other Bluetooth platforms (My PC etc) I've tried clearing the caches and force-stopping of all of the Bluetooth-related apps, then clearing the overall cache and rebooting. A Youtube video for a similar problem on a different brand of phone recommended that. Again, it seemed to work. Then it stopped working, and now doesn't even affect it. I tried going into recovery mode an deleting the cache partition. No effect. I've tried clearing the network configuration. No effect. I've tried third-party apps that promised more control over Bluetooth if not an actual remedy, no good. Yes, I've consulted the manual. It doesn't say much about Bluetooth.

To be frank about BLU customer service, I can't tell if they understand me. I definitely don't understand half of what they say.

I did find one app that says it will remedy the exact problem. That's the only thing I found that mentions this malfunction specifically, and it's for a much earlier version of Android. I might have tried it anyway . . . except I have to root my phone first, and I'm not going there.

So, partially to get your attention, I give this phone 1/5, since I want a working Bluetooth. Also the malfunction is so aggravating, and I've put in a lot of futile hours trying to correct what would seem to be a minor issue.
