Solid upgrade from the Note 10+. *Updated* For the record, I was very unsure of this upgrade. I have been a Note user for the last 10 years. I have never owned an S Series device and I had a lot of hesitancy to make this change. Two things won me over to at least try it: First, the likelihood of a new Note this year is slim and if I really missed the S Pen I could still use one here. Second, I have been very excited to own a 120hz display and didn't want to wait another year to get one. Frankly, I really just wanted to try it out and had no real confidence I would keep it. Well, I am going to be keeping it and, surprisingly, it isn't because it is head and shoulders above the Note in any particular way. It's just that it is a little better in every possible way and the totality of those improvements make the S21 Ultra a worthy upgrade. Here are some of the areas the Ultra really shines:

-The Screen: First off, all Samsung devices have amazing screens so we don't even need to talk about the quality of the image. However, Samsung has packed some new tech into the Ultra when comparing it to prior years. The S21 Ultra has an adaptive refresh rate that can crank out 120hz but also slow all the way down to 10hz. Unlike last year's Ultra, you can run the adaptive refresh rate on the max resolution of 1440. The combination is amazing and once you get scrolling or watch a great show on Netflix, it just cannot be unseen. Amazing! I actually find myself mesmerized at times. The ability to get down to 10hz really saves battery as well. It is very well executed. Speaking of battery, this panel is a low energy consumption panel. I read how it works and won't bore you with the details but, suffice to say, this is another first and it too helps with your battery life. You can set the screen to classic Samsung vivid display or one that is more natural. No matter which one you choose, you will be very happy looking at this phone every day.

-Form Factor: This phone looks amazing. Period! All color variations come with a flat matte finish. I went with the black and couldn't be happier. The black is so cool, in fact, that Samsung created a 3 minute video explaining how it is made. Google "Galaxy S21 Ultra: Untold Stories – Phantom Black" and unleash your inner geek. In spite of having a matte finish that feels almost metal, it is actually Gorilla Glass Victus. Both sides of the phone are so you get improved scratch and crack resistance. The camera array wraps around the body from the frame. As one reviewer I read put it, "If you are going to have a huge camera bump, you might as well embrace it and make it great." Samsung did just that. The power and volume button are where they belong on the right side. I took my case off (boo) to snap these photos with a coworker's phone and she gasped and said, "that phone is sweet!" She is a much younger coworker but I couldn't agree with her more.

-Battery Life: Samsung packs a 5000mah battery in the S21 Ultra and, when mated with aforementioned display enhancements and the all new Qualcomm 888 chipset, is pretty easily an all day phone. I am seeing reviewers say that they are getting a day and a half and even two days. I don't know how they use their phones but I am not seeing that performance. Frankly, it really isn't much better than my Note. I would say that it is more predictable. This is the first phone I have ever owned that, in just the week I have owned it, I always know that no matter what I throw at this, my battery will hold up. Not groundbreaking but very solid.

-The Cameras: I am not going to cover the camera system at length here as I would be here all day writing and there are a ton of reviews out there detailing what Samsung has done here. Suffice to say, Samsung has a a very good camera set up here. I took a 30x zoom photo of my son when we were sledding and included for you guys to see. I was on top of the sledding hill and he was at the bottom. I was probably 60 yards or so away. I broke out my phone, freezing on the top of the hill, zoomed in, and fired off a shot. It looks like I am right in front of him almost. Not a perfect image by any means but truly amazing nonetheless. In other real world use, I find night mode to work well and the video it produces is amazing. You can shoot 8k but the 4k at 60fps is the way to go. Really though, if you're like me and just want to be able to pull out your camera, aim, shoot, and know that you are going to get a high quality photo every time, the S21 Ultra is a great choice. I haven't taken a bad picture yet.

-Intangibles: The S21 Ultra is Samsung's first non-Note that can utilize the S-Pen. You will need to buy a case that can accommodate it. It isn't a perfect set up for me but it does work just like a Note. I am waiting to see what Samsung does with the S-Pen Pro that is slated for a likely late summer release before I buy the current $69 silicone case with S-Pen accessory they are offering. Samsung, like Apple, no longer includes a brick or headphones. I have plenty of bricks so that isn't an issue for me but I love those little USBC AKG headphones Samsung used to throw in darn it! The built in speakers are solid and improved over my Note. The Ultra does have High Res audio out via USBC if you don't mind a cord. The phone does have the latest Bluetooth 5.2 /LE and Wifi 6E standards. Lastly, the 888 chipset supports all three 5G standards so you should be able to keep up as the 5G networks continue to grow.

-Conclusion: As I said in the beginning of my review, this isn't a particularly ground breaking device. Frankly, it is a nod to the Note 10+ how close these devices really are in real world use. They even cut out expandable memory on the S21 series! Ugh!! Even with all of that, I am completely happy with this upgrade. It just does everything a little bit better than the Note. Further, and this is a big one, unlike the Note, Samsung has really future proofed this phone. With access to all 5G standards, the latest 888 chipset with 5nm architecture, 6E Wifi (which isn't even really out yet in any meaningful way), both Bluetooth 5.2 and LE, 16GB of RAM (holy overkill), the latest 3.1 UFS storage, and so much more. There is just no way that two years from now, you will feel like you have an old phone. Oh, and I forgot to mention, Samsung did this and managed to shave $200 off of last years prices which isn't insignificant. If you want a blazing fast head turning phone that you wont need to upgrade anytime soon and can do way more than you will ever ask it to, the Samsung S21 Ultra should be on the top of your list.

*Update on battery* It is better than I originally thought. It took a few days for the new phone to identify all the apps it needed to put to sleep. Now that it has, I am beginning to see strong battery life here. I have the Ultra pretty maxed out. Using 1440 WQHD+ display with full adaptive screen tech, I am over 7 hours on screen including almost 2 hours using Waze which just sucks battery life. I still have 23% battery life. Not game changing but really impressive. More to come.

*Update* Okay, so the battery continues to impress. Been off charger since 6:15am today. Used Waze for 90 minutes, watched two hours on HBO Max, and used my phone normally the rest of the day. It is 8:00pm and I am sitting at 46%. This is much better than my Note which would be hanging by a thread now. One other thing I want to point out is that Samsung really did a nice job with the oleophobic coating on the screen. It is really thick and nice to the touch. I have always felt like Samsung was way behind Apple in this arena. Not anymore. Solid. This is a great phone. More to come.

Okay, one more thought that don't think I emphasized enough in my initial review is with regard to speed. This phone is crazy fast. Like it almost knows what you want to do before you do it. I know Apple fan, I hear you. Your chipset is still faster. That is true. It wins most of the benchmark tests. Some quite handily. However, after sitting down and playing around with my wife's iPhone 12 Pro, it really doesn't feel that way. After all, current Apple flagships have a 60hz display still. The 12 Pro may be capable of a bit more but in real world use it feels sluggish. It was actually somewhat painful honestly. It looks great, of course, because Apple is using an older Samsung display but, once you start opening apps and scrolling around, the 12 Pro really feels like an old device when compared to the speed the S21 Ultra unleashes. I would make this analogy that some of you guys will get. You can buy or build the best gaming PC ever made. If you put it on an old monitor with a 60hz refresh rate, you will still be able to use it but it just won't look or feel as good as it could once the battle begins. Fire up a faster display and it will begin to feel like the gaming machine you invested in. My point is that, while the iPhone 12 Pro is a very capable phone, it doesn't have the screen to maximize its potential. The Ultra is capable and has a screen to match its horsepower. If you can't tell, I have fallen for this phone. So good. Buy it with confidence.

It's just that it is a little better in every possible way and the totality of those improvements make the S21 Ultra a worthy upgrade. Here are some of the areas the Ultra really shines:

-The Screen: First off, all Samsung devices have amazing screens so we don't even need to talk about the quality of the image. However, Samsung has packed some new tech into the Ultra when comparing it to prior years. The S21 Ultra has an adaptive refresh rate that can crank out 120hz but also slow all the way down to 10hz. Unlike last year's Ultra, you can run the adaptive refresh rate on the max resolution of 1440. The combination is amazing and once you get scrolling or watch a great show on Netflix, it just cannot be unseen. Amazing! I actually find myself mesmerized at times. The ability to get down to 10hz really saves battery as well. It is very well executed. Speaking of battery, this panel is a low energy consumption panel. I read how it works and won't bore you with the details but, suffice to say, this is another first and it too helps with your battery life. You can set the screen to classic Samsung vivid display or one that is more natural. No matter which one you choose, you will be very happy looking at this phone every day.

-Form Factor: This phone looks amazing. Period! All color variations come with a flat matte finish. I went with the black and couldn't be happier. The black is so cool, in fact, that Samsung created a 3 minute video explaining how it is made. Google "Galaxy S21 Ultra: Untold Stories – Phantom Black" and unleash your inner geek. In spite of having a matte finish that feels almost metal, it is actually Gorilla Glass Victus. Both sides of the phone are so you get improved scratch and crack resistance. The camera array wraps around the body from the frame. As one reviewer I read put it, "If you are going to have a huge camera bump, you might as well embrace it and make it great." Samsung did just that. The power and volume button are where they belong on the right side. I took my case off (boo) to snap these photos with a coworker's phone and she gasped and said, "that phone is sweet!" She is a much younger coworker but I couldn't agree with her more.

-Battery Life: Samsung packs a 5000mah battery in the S21 Ultra and, when mated with aforementioned display enhancements and the all new Qualcomm 888 chipset, is pretty easily an all day phone. I am seeing reviewers say that they are getting a day and a half and even two days. I don't know how they use their phones but I am not seeing that performance. Frankly, it really isn't much better than my Note. I would say that it is more predictable. This is the first phone I have ever owned that, in just the week I have owned it, I always know that no matter what I throw at this, my battery will hold up. Not groundbreaking but very solid.

-The Cameras: I am not going to cover the camera system at length here as I would be here all day writing and there are a ton of reviews out there detailing what Samsung has done here. Suffice to say, Samsung has a a very good camera set up here. I took a 30x zoom photo of my son when we were sledding and included for you guys to see. I was on top of the sledding hill and he was at the bottom. I was probably 60 yards or so away. I broke out my phone, freezing on the top of the hill, zoomed in, and fired off a shot. It looks like I am right in front of him almost. Not a perfect image by any means but truly amazing nonetheless. In other real world use, I find night mode to work well and the video it produces is amazing. You can shoot 8k but the 4k at 60fps is the way to go. Really though, if you're like me and just want to be able to pull out your camera, aim, shoot, and know that you are going to get a high quality photo every time, the S21 Ultra is a great choice. I haven't taken a bad picture yet.

-Intangibles: The S21 Ultra is Samsung's first non-Note that can utilize the S-Pen. You will need to buy a case that can accommodate it. It isn't a perfect set up for me but it does work just like a Note. I am waiting to see what Samsung does with the S-Pen Pro that is slated for a likely late summer release before I buy the current $69 silicone case with S-Pen accessory they are offering. Samsung, like Apple, no longer includes a brick or headphones. I have plenty of bricks so that isn't an issue for me but I love those little USBC AKG headphones Samsung used to throw in darn it! The built in speakers are solid and improved over my Note. The Ultra does have High Res audio out via USBC if you don't mind a cord. The phone does have the latest Bluetooth 5.2 /LE and Wifi 6E standards. Lastly, the 888 chipset supports all three 5G standards so you should be able to keep up as the 5G networks continue to grow.

-Conclusion: As I said in the beginning of my review, this isn't a particularly ground breaking device. Frankly, it is a nod to the Note 10+ how close these devices really are in real world use. They even cut out expandable memory on the S21 series! Ugh!! Even with all of that, I am completely happy with this upgrade. It just does everything a little bit better than the Note. Further, and this is a big one, unlike the Note, Samsung has really future proofed this phone. With access to all 5G standards, the latest 888 chipset with 5nm architecture, 6E Wifi (which isn't even really out yet in any meaningful way), both Bluetooth 5.2 and LE, 16GB of RAM (holy overkill), the latest 3.1 UFS storage, and so much more. There is just no way that two years from now, you will feel like you have an old phone. Oh, and I forgot to mention, Samsung did this and managed to shave $200 off of last years prices which isn't insignificant. If you want a blazing fast head turning phone that you wont need to upgrade anytime soon and can do way more than you will ever ask it to, the Samsung S21 Ultra should be on the top of your list.

*Update on battery* It is better than I originally thought. It took a few days for the new phone to identify all the apps it needed to put to sleep. Now that it has, I am beginning to see strong battery life here. I have the Ultra pretty maxed out. Using 1440 WQHD+ display with full adaptive screen tech, I am over 7 hours on screen including almost 2 hours using Waze which just sucks battery life. I still have 23% battery life. Not game changing but really impressive. More to come.

*Update* Okay, so the battery continues to impress. Been off charger since 6:15am today. Used Waze for 90 minutes, watched two hours on HBO Max, and used my phone normally the rest of the day. It is 8:00pm and I am sitting at 46%. This is much better than my Note which would be hanging by a thread now. One other thing I want to point out is that Samsung really did a nice job with the oleophobic coating on the screen. It is really thick and nice to the touch. I have always felt like Samsung was way behind Apple in this arena. Not anymore. Solid. This is a great phone. More to come.

Okay, one more thought that don't think I emphasized enough in my initial review is with regard to speed. This phone is crazy fast. Like it almost knows what you want to do before you do it. I know Apple fan, I hear you. Your chipset is still faster. That is true. It wins most of the benchmark tests. Some quite handily. However, after sitting down and playing around with my wife's iPhone 12 Pro, it really doesn't feel that way. After all, current Apple flagships have a 60hz display still. The 12 Pro may be capable of a bit more but in real world use it feels sluggish. It was actually somewhat painful honestly. It looks great, of course, because Apple is using an older Samsung display but, once you start opening apps and scrolling around, the 12 Pro really feels like an old device when compared to the speed the S21 Ultra unleashes. I would make this analogy that some of you guys will get. You can buy or build the best gaming PC ever made. If you put it on an old monitor with a 60hz refresh rate, you will still be able to use it but it just won't look or feel as good as it could once the battle begins. Fire up a faster display and it will begin to feel like the gaming machine you invested in. My point is that, while the iPhone 12 Pro is a very capable phone, it doesn't have the screen to maximize its potential. The Ultra is capable and has a screen to match its horsepower. If you can't tell, I have fallen for this phone. So good. Buy it with confidence.

Had to purchase charge port replacements twice for the Life One X2's (each). Though mine have never had issues as I only have to charge my phone once or twice a week (don't do social media). My One X2 lasted 2 years and I'm now using a Blu XL3 Plus.

The camera is its "best/worst" feature Depending on your tastes, the camera on the s21u is both really good and really bad. If you can get over some of the auto-correcting features/high light bloom, it can get some pretty darn cool shots. Heck, you can now take pictures of the moon through its phases. The main thing is trying to get a clear and unblurred shot on normal photo mode isn't easy. It will track movement and then take the picture about .03-.12 seconds AFTER the preview photo's image, so you're not getting that exact moment, which can either be good or bad.

Phone basic functionality - Texting and calling can do a lot better. S20 and after seem to have a very funky way of handling both due to 5g not really being a widespread thing, but even set to wifi they can't seem to hold a signal very well for either. Repeated messages etc. Fortunately for me, I don't use either enough for it to be an issue.

Battery/cpu - It will start putting all apps that like to start in the background to a hibernate status if you never use them, I quite like this feature. The one thing is under cpu strain like a game or something, or just sitting in your pocket, it can get quite warm-> actually hot. Just make sure to avoid programs that do this.

The screen is very nice, 120hz on a phone vs a pc, there's a world of difference for smoothness on a phone. No issues here, and it isn't bad on standard 60 either.

Overall, 5g(the service) is still vastly overrated. But the phone itself, is definitely not.

I can’t believe how lucky my boyfriend got. Ignore the smudges on the second photo, those are not scratches.

My boyfriend wanted a newer phone, we were nervous, we bought it anyway. The condition of this phone is AMAZING. He ordered the 64GB, blue. There are roughly 6 cosmetic issues and I don’t even want to call them cosmetic issues. They’re so tiny on the back of the phone, it looks like someone took a sewing needle and simply POKED the phone. They aren’t even noticeable unless you’re deliberately checking for imperfections and the phone is practically on your nose. I’ve seen worse done with brand new phones from shipping.

Now, the new iOS updates allows you to go into settings to find non genuine parts like displays, batteries, cameras, etc. This phone doesn’t pop for a SINGLE off brand part. Every single part in this phone seems to fully check out to apple or simply have not even been replaced.

I even went farther and logged into my apple support. The phone was first purchased in 2020, and hasn’t had a single pop up there for unauthenticated parts either. Further boosting us into loving the idea that this phone is all Apple.

The camera works perfectly and the battery health is at 84% which is a great health rate for him, and a used phone in general.

The phone was also entirely unlocked. I didn’t have to pay anything to turn it on, I was able to use my old SIM card, and it was fully set up to my carrier MOMENTS after restarting the phone.

The only thing I didn’t check was the light in the sim port for water damage. But with how wonderful this phone is, I’m not even bothering taking the sim back out to check.

Extremely lucky buy, or extremely great sellers. Who knows, but we’re thankful.
Whoever this phone was bought from, amazing person. Whoever “fixed” this phone, amazing person. We couldn’t be happier purchasing this. Especially it being the first time we bought refurbished, ever.
